To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aminophospho lipids are asymmetrically distributed in murine synaptosome plasma membranes and that the fatty acyl composition of the outer monolayers of the synaptosome plasma membrane differs from that of the inner monolayer.
aminophospho‐lipid asymmetry exists in the plasma membrane of synaptosomes, that the asymmetry is independent of the exchange of lipids with serum‐lipoproteins, and that the asymmetry exists in vivo.
aminophosphoglipid asymmetry in brain synaptosomes is not dependent on the presence of lipoproteins and is not dependent on methylation reactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of the aminophosphatide asymmetry in synaptoplasmic membranes.
the role of aminophosholipids in the maintenance of membrane asymmetry and the possible involvement of these lipids in synaptic transmission.
the role of aminophosholipids in synaptic function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphatidethanolamines in the inner monolayer of mouse synaptosomal plasma mem‐branes are not in a methylated state and are not derived from the serum lipoproteins.
the aminophospho lipids in synaptosomal membranes are asymmetrically distributed in the bilayer and that this asymmetric distribution does not require the presence of serum‐lipopro teins.
aminophosphoglycerides in the outer monolyer of the synaptosomes plasma membrane were not the products of phosphatidylcholine‐methylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aminophosphatidylethanelamine is distributed asymmetrically in synaptosomal membrane and this distribution is independent of the methylating enzyme.
the aminophosphoglipid asymmetry is a property of the plasma membrane of the synaptosome.
the asymmetry of aminophopholipids is a fundamental property of biological membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use the mouse as a new model system to study the role of aminophosoholipid asymmetries in the brain and in the nervous system.

we have developed a chemical labeling technique for the determination of aminophospolipid distribution in biological membranes that is independent of phospholipase A2 activity and of serum‐lipid exchange processes.
the phospholipid asymmetries in synaptosomes and synaptosomal plasma‐membrane vesicles are not a result of serum‐lipid exchange processes or phosphatidyletanolamine‐metylating enzymes.
